It is modeled mathematically as f(d) = e^{-α|d|}, where α governs the rate of decline. This implies a dual structure: one where deviation from the original stimulus reduces response strength, and another where symmetry ensures equal influence on either side of the stimulus axis. The empirical fit R(d) = A·e^{-βd²} introduces a quadratic correction to better match experimental data, suggesting non-linear sensitivity near the origin. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient sample size or misalignment of stimulus dimensions, leading to incorrect generalization boundaries. The symmetric nature also implies that any deviation in either direction contributes equally to the overall response reduction, enforcing a balanced cognitive processing model.
